body:
Four clicks tell you what your ad is chasing.

Most people never check this. They judge the ad by the creative, the image or video everyone spent hours on. That's the wrong screen.

The screen that matters is Ads Manager, at the ad set level, the line called Performance goal. It tells you what Meta is actually optimising for — leads, messages, or something else entirely.

If that line doesn't match what you want to happen after someone clicks, no creative fixes it. Meta will keep sending you the wrong people, fast, and cheap, and confidently.

Across the accounts we've handled, 7,341 people have filled a lead form. Every one of those started because Meta was chasing a specific goal, set on a specific screen, before a single ad ran.

Check the goal before you touch the creative. It decides who Meta goes and finds.

If you want to see how your own account is set up, an audit is free on jothiswaroop.com.

slides.text: Four clicks tell you what your ad is chasing.
Most people judge it by the creative. Wrong screen entirely.
Open Ads Manager. Click into the campaign you want to check.
Click one level down, into the ad set inside it.
Find the line called Performance goal. Most people never open this.
This line tells Meta what to chase — leads, messages, something else.
Say it's set to messages, but you actually want form fills.
Meta will keep sending people who message, not people who fill forms.
No creative fixes a mismatch here. Not the image, not the copy.
Check this before the creative. It decides who Meta goes and finds.
